Grace period: Washington sets no grace period for rent, which is due when the lease says. What it sets is a bar on late fees for rent paid within five days after the due date; you may still serve a 14-day pay-or-vacate notice any time after rent is due (`edu-late-fee-wa`).

title: Checked Across the Whole Washington Code: Squatters, Receipts, Registration and Out-of-State Owners
bodyText: The whole RCW, the held WAC titles, the Constitution, the 2025-2026 session laws and the saved court rules, not only the landlord-tenant chapters, were searched for these. (1) Squatters: present. For a person who isn't and hasn't been a tenant, a lawful occupant or an owner, you may give police a sworn declaration in the statutory form, and an officer may remove the person; it can't be used against a tenant or a tenant's guests (`edu-unauthorized-occupants-wa`, `edu-trespass-notice-wa`). (2) Rent receipts: present. You may refuse cash, but if you accept it you must give a receipt, and you must give a written receipt for any other payment on request (`edu-rent-receipts-wa`). (3) Landlord registration: no statewide registration or license for residential landlords; cities may require one, and manufactured/mobile home communities register separately (`edu-no-landlord-registration-wa`). (4) Out-of-state LLCs and corporations: a foreign entity doing business in Washington can't maintain an action, an eviction included, until it registers and pays the fees and penalties for its unregistered years; leases stay valid and it can still defend (`edu-nonresident-owner-agent-wa`). (5) Trade names: if you rent under a name that isn't your true name, register it with the Department of Revenue; until you do you can't maintain a suit, though you can defend one (`edu-no-landlord-registration-wa`). (6) Owners who live elsewhere: name an agent living in the county for notices and process, or the person you pay rent to is treated as that agent (`landlord-disclosure-wa`); owning property here or breaking the landlord-tenant act submits you to Washington's courts (`edu-nonresident-owner-agent-wa`). (7) Reporting duties: none binds you as a landlord, but some bind everyone, you included: notifying officials as soon as reasonably possible after witnessing a violent offense, a sexual offense against a child or a serious assault on a child, and notifying the coroner, medical examiner or police of human remains (`edu-law-enforcement-cooperation-wa`). This search did not cover city or county ordinances or case law.

title: Checks Marked 'Paid in Full'
bodyText: Washington follows the Uniform Commercial Code rule on checks marked 'paid in full' (RCW 62A.3-311). If a tenant, or anyone else you have a claim against, gives you a check or other payment instrument for less than you claim, with a conspicuous statement, on the check or in a writing with it, that it is offered in full satisfaction of the claim, then cashing it settles your whole claim, the unpaid balance included. This applies only when the payment was offered in good faith and the amount was not yet fixed or was subject to a genuine (bona fide) dispute, so writing 'paid in full' on a short check for rent nobody disputes does not by itself settle the rent owed. Writing 'under protest' or 'without prejudice' when you endorse the check does not save the balance: the rule on reserving your rights does not apply to an accord and satisfaction (RCW 62A.1-308(b)). There are two ways out. If you are an organization (for example an LLC) and, within a reasonable time before the check, sent the tenant a conspicuous statement that communications about disputed debts, including checks offered in full satisfaction, must go to a named person, office or place, the claim is not settled if the check or the writing with it was not received there. And whether or not you are an organization, the claim is not settled if you offer to repay the amount of the check within 90 days after it is paid; an organization that sent the statement just described cannot use this second way out. Neither way out works if you, or your agent responsible for the disputed debt, knew within a reasonable time before the check was collected that it was offered in full satisfaction. The cautious course: don't cash a check for less than you claim that is marked as payment in full of a disputed amount; return it, and if one is cashed by mistake, offer the money back within 90 days.

title: Duty of Good Faith
bodyText: Washington's landlord-tenant act imposes a duty of good faith: every duty under the chapter, and every act that must be done before using a right or remedy under it, carries an obligation of good faith in its performance or enforcement (RCW 59.18.020). That binds you and the tenant alike. In practice: give notices, enter, handle the deposit, enforce lease terms and end a tenancy honestly and for the purpose the law or the lease gives you the right, not as a pretext.
